title: Staggered service flip cheatsheet
content:
Purpose: quick reference + working notes for doing a staggered service flip (multi-tenant aware) — emphasis on quiet traffic windows, predictable warmup, and tenant isolation. NOT a formal runbook; this is my scratchpad for experiments and heuristics.

Top-level goals:
- keep tail latency stable (< target SLO + small buffer)
- avoid cache-tsunami (massive KV misses)
- ensure per-tenant rollback is possible without global disruption
- collect repeatable telemetry for warmup effectiveness

Quick checklist (preflight):
- ✅ confirm baseline telemetry for last 7 days: p50/p95/p99, error rate, cold-KV-miss rate
- ✅ identify anchor tenants (top 10 by QPS and top 10 by spend) -> mark as "no-flip" or staged first
- ✅ ensure canary image/model variant is pinned and tagged (image sha + model hash)
- ✅ run smoke tests in staging with traffic-replay of representative requests (10k/min target sim)
- ✅ coordinate quiet window with infra & SRE (preferred 02:00–06:00 local region)
- ✅ pre-warm caches for high-frequency prefixes for anchor tenants
- ✅ notify on-call and create ephemeral incident channel (Slack thread)

Traffic shaping plan (staggered service flip):
- Phase 0 (priming): 0% -> 0% (dry run) — health checks only for 10m
- Phase 1 (micro-cohort): route 0.5% traffic from non-anchor tenants for 15m; watch tail latency + KV miss spike; keep CPU/GPU utilization under monitoring thresholds (see thresholds)
- Phase 2 (capped ramp): 0.5% -> 5% over 30m, increment 0.5% every 3m; check signals each step
- Phase 3 (cohort expansion): 5% -> 25% over 2h, only add cohorts with "good" telemetry in last 30m
- Phase 4 (broadening): 25% -> 60% over 4h with automated backoff on negative signals
- Phase 5 (cutover): 60% -> 100% in 2h if stable; otherwise hold and investigate

Per-tenant pinning/affinity rules:
- Anchor tenants: require opt-in and manual approval for flip OR run on dedicated pool; default = do not flip without owner ok
- High-sensitivity tenants (latency-sensitive): sticky routing to old variant for 24–48h after cutover until warm caches observed
- New tenants or low-volume: prefer to include in early micro-cohort to gather warming data
- Override list: a short-lived flag in runtime to pin a tenant to a version for emergency rollback (TTL 6h)

Warmup heuristics (model + runtime):
- Warm top-10 prefixes observed over last 24h into KV before routing traffic; use sampling to avoid overpopulating cache
- For models with large KV state, pre-fetch top-1% hot keys per tenant (estimate using heatmap job)
- If quantized variant: pre-run 50 inference calls per GPU to populate runtime kernels and lazy-compile caches
- For sequence-length sensitive workloads, inject synthetic short and long sequences (2x) to exercise both fast/slow paths

Telemetry signals to watch (immediate + rolling):
- Immediate (1–5m): increase in 5xx, lat spikes > 2x p95 baseline, sudden GPU mem pressure alerts
- Short rolling (15–60m): CPU/GPU utilization approaching 85% sustained, KV miss rate > baseline + 30%, error-rate change > +0.2pp
- Business (hours): user-visible error tickets, usage drop from anchor tenants, latency regressions correlating with cohort time

Automated safety/backoff rules (to implement or verify before flip):
- If p99 > baseline * 1.4 for 3 consecutive windows => automatic 50% reduction of traffic to candidate variant and alert
- If 5xx increase by > 100% absolute or > 0.5pp => immediate cut to 0% for that tenant cohort and page SRE
- If KV miss rate spike > 5x baseline in 10m => throttle input concurrency for new variant and start graceful fallback to cached results

Runbook snippets (for quick ops):
- Quick rollback (per-tenant): flip sticky flag for tenant -> re-route via legacy pool; verify success by p95/p99 returning to baseline for that tenant
- Global rollback: route 100% to previous pool via global routing policy; abort further expansion; do a diagnostic snapshot (top failing request ids, top keys missing)
- Emergency throttle: set per-instance concurrency to N=50% of max for 10m; revert once heat reduces

Open questions / things to experiment:
- How effective is pre-fetching hot keys vs. gradual traffic in real tenants? (A/B test: tenant cohort A pre-warm, B not)
- Best warmup volume for quantized models to minimize JIT/compile overhead without wasting GPU cycles
- Evaluate whether synthetic warm requests degrade QPS accounting for customers (we need clear metering)
- Can we create a cheap approximate predictor for which tenants will cause cache storms (based on recent churn + prefix entropy)?

Notes to self (TLDNR):
- Start very small, prioritize observability, protect anchors.
- Prefer staged micro cohorts over blunt 10% jumps.
- Keep rollback cheap and per-tenant where possible.

Post-flip checklist (first 24h):
- Run warmup effectiveness job at 1h, 6h, 24h and compare KV hit rate and p95 per tenant
- Confirm no regression in top-20 tenants (latency + errors)
- Collect logs for any tenants that required rollback — capture request ids and key heatmaps
- Retrospective notes in Confluence with embedding of critical metrics and decision timeline

Short cheat-cards (for on-call):
- If tail latency -> backoff to previous variant for cohort and open incident thread
- If KV miss tsunami -> throttle new variant, enable fallback cache layer, and pre-warm high-frequency keys
- If anchor tenant issues -> escalate to PM/SE, hold expansion, and schedule dedicated deep-dive

TODOs (me):
- [ ] add small script to generate pre-warm key list from heatmap job (pri: high)
- [ ] implement per-tenant TTL pin flag in runtime (small API) (pri: med)
- [ ] add telemetry dashboards: "staggered-flip overview" and "per-cohort heatmap" (pri: med)
- [ ] run first internal experiment with safe cohort next Tue (coordinate with Priya)

Random scribbles:
- observed that 1% early cohort often shows disproportionate KV-miss signal because of tail keys; consider seeding with synthetic duplicates of heavy keys to amortize cost
- remember to suppress noisy alarms during expected warm spikes (annotate alert rules)

End of scratchpad. Keep this lean and copy into a proper playbook once we validate the approach.
summary: Working notes and heuristics for a staggered multi-tenant service flip: preflight, traffic phases, warmup rules, telemetry signals, backoff rules, per-tenant pinning, and immediate runbook snippets. Draft/scratchpad for eng-serving-runtime.
